text:
Samir Kaur: Heads up — AriaHealth wants a performance validation before procurement — target sustained 5k QPS for patient-summary generation. They expect short tails: p95 < 180ms for <=150-token responses. Also ask for variance during 30s spikes (they mentioned traffic due to morning reports).

Liam Wong: Clarify workload mix: full-text generation (templated medical summaries) with ~5% embeddings for search and 2% long-form summaries (~800 tokens). If 5k QPS includes the long-form, GPU counts spike.

Nora Blake: Suggested test pattern: 10m ramp to 5k, 20m sustain, then three 30s spikes at +200% at 7, 14, 18 minutes into sustain, then cool down. Capture p50/p90/p95/p99, error rate, and per-request token counts. Collect host/GPU metrics and request traces.

Liam Wong: Example k6 job (pseudo):

```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';

export let options = {
  stages: [
    { duration: '10m', target: 5000 },
    { duration: '20m', target: 5000 },
    { duration: '5m', target: 0 },
  ],
  thresholds: { 'http_req_duration{p95}': ['p(95)<180'] }
};

export default function() {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat', JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'patient_summary' }), { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${__ENV.TOKEN}` } });
  sleep(0.0002);
}
```

SecOps: Security checklist — AriaHealth requires data-in-transit + at-rest encryption, SOC2 reports, and proof of key separation. They also asked whether we support VPC endpoints and if logs can be routed to their SIEM. For BYOK with HSM they will need Private.

Samir Kaur: Procurement wants two commercial scenarios: 1) 1-month reserved Dedicated pool estimate with burst credits, 2) hosted on-demand estimate. Also add a 6-month committed option if rates drop. Please include expected RU (request unit) or token consumption cost and an ops SLA add-on for latency SLO.

Nora Blake: Perf sizing quick calc: baseline 5k * avg 150 tokens = 750k tokens/s. For our 30B-style model at FP16 with good batching we estimate ~5-7 A100 equiv for steady state; with 4-bit quantization maybe 3-5. Long-form requests will spike memory and may force sharding — plan to isolate long-form traffic on a separate route.

Liam Wong: Actioning a sim tonight across perf cluster. I'll run two profiles: (A) mixed (95% short, 5% long) and (B) short-only. Will collect GPU/s host load and tail latencies. ETA: post results by 11:15 PT tomorrow.

DevTestBot: benchmark scheduled: aria-poc-4301237000 (runner: perf-bastion-3).

SecOps: For the security questionnaire I'll prepare answers for hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and list required lead times for HSM. Also include certificate rotation notes.

Ops Lead: Ops runbook items: reserve stage dedicated pool min=3 max=10; pre-warm caches; route long-form to a dedicated node pool to avoid KV thrash. Set alerts: p95>250ms and error-rate>0.5%.

Liam Wong: Pricing inputs for finance — need expected token split prompt vs completion, and percent of requests that are long-form. Samir, can you confirm with the buyer?

Samir Kaur: Confirmed: expected mix 80% short (prompt 40 / completion 100 avg), 15% medium (250 tokens), 5% long (~800 tokens). They also expect 4% of traffic to call embeddings (small vectors).

Nora Blake: With that mix effective avg tokens/request ≈ 190. Recalc: 5k * 190 ≈ 950k tokens/s. Sizing likely increases by ~30% vs earlier estimate. I'll post a refined GPU estimate after the sim.

Liam Wong: Quick note on experiment config: we'll pin exact model binary and disable background auto-warm. Use consistent seed prompts and deterministic decoding for latency stability.

Samir Kaur: Scheduling a 45m alignment call with AriaHealth for tomorrow 8:30am PT — include SecOps and Ops. Also sharing questionnaire and sample prompt set in the calendar invite.

DevTestBot: run started: aria-poc-4301237000 (job id: 9307). ETA ~40m.

Nora Blake: After sim, we'll produce a short report: summary, latency CDF plots, GPU utilization heatmap, expected committed pricing (1mo/6mo), and recommended config (Dedicated pool size, caching, split routes). I'll draft and share for review.

Liam Wong: No blockers from perf side, kicking off now.

SecOps: I'll review the questionnaire draft and add the SIEM/logging flow diagram.

Samir Kaur: Thanks team — let's aim to have the draft report + draft quote ready before the sync. If anything urgent pops up ping here.

Ops Lead: FYI — if you see OOMs during long-form spikes, reduce token parallelism and ramp slower.

Samir Kaur: Closing notes: deliverables before meeting: perf sim results (Liam), draft security answers (SecOps), staging pool reserved (Ops Lead), pricing draft (finance/sales).

Samir Kaur: Thanks all :)
